items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: but he worked on Keith's Circuit too

ctx.x: So man, I told him -- cut that -- (Recording interruption) So now we're in New York and we're just gigging, nothing steady, so we get a job -- Wilbur Sweatman, he was vaudeville, he played three clarinets at one time, but he used a piano and a trumpet and drums. So he had this engagement at the Lafayette Theatre and so I got that gig for us. I got that for us, we played around New York, in New Jersey

but he worked on Keith's Circuit too, but it was just four of us on the stage and him and he played clarinet, three of them at one time. Beautiful. Stage setting, he had a beautiful stage setting, whole lot of drapes, but we used to have to get to the theatre an hour before showtime to get made up.

Boy, when we come on that stage, we waslight as a sheet of newspaper, ain't no way in the world you could tell us. Everybody was light -- like Willie Bryant -- did you ever see Willie Bryant, no. He used to be at that Apollo, He looked like a /white boy, light as Tizol. You saw Tizol.
